assets.reliability: Codes have a four-module quiet zone unless margin sets 0 to 16, and need a contrast of at least 4.5 between modules and tile; some older scanners read only dark-on-light codes. A rendered file does not prove that every printer or camera reads it; test the final output.
assets.text: Render the same QR code as the website without a browser, as SVG, PNG or JPG. The qr2g.it logo is on by default; logo=false leaves it out. The API also renders presentation, poster, label and badge presets.
assets.title: QR codes

automation.batch: Create or reuse up to 25 repositories in one request. Each entry has its own outcome or error and costs one unit of quota.
automation.quota: Read today's quota without spending it. A 429 quota_exceeded answer carries Retry-After until the next UTC day.
automation.text: Coding agents and scripts use a revocable token issued by the operator instead of the browser check. Repeating a creation request returns the same canonical link, so retries are safe. Every response carries X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset.
automation.title: Automation tokens

docs.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select and copy the command instead.

create.result: The response is JSON: 201 for a newly created link or 200 for an existing one. Unknown, private, or invalid repositories are rejected.
create.text: POST a complete HTTPS GitHub repository URL. The shorthand command above is the simplest option for terminal use.
create.title: Submit JSON
create.verification: POST requests require a fresh Turnstile token from a browser challenge. Set TURNSTILE_TOKEN to that single-use token.

explore.stats: Read daily filtered redirects for a listed repository. They exclude HEAD requests, identifiable bots, previews and API traffic, and are not unique people.
explore.text: Search listed repositories with pagination. Only repositories submitted to qr2g.it that are public and not opted out appear.
explore.title: Listed repositories and statistics
explore.top: The most visited listed repositories over the last 30 days, with daily counts, their total and the time of the latest counted redirect. The home page shows the top three.

docs.guide: Markdown usage guide for agents and chats

inspect.info: A plus sign after the slug returns the same metadata. Slugs use uppercase base36; keep their case.
inspect.lookup: Find the existing link of a repository without creating one and without a GitHub call. A missing link answers 404 link_not_found.
inspect.text: Read stored metadata without contacting GitHub. Replace 2 with your slug. The JSON includes the initial and current repository names, destination, state, and verification times.
inspect.title: Inspect a link

docs.intro: Create, inspect and export links with curl, scripts or coding agents.

limits.errors: Errors contain a stable error code and a message. Use --fail-with-body to keep the JSON response while making curl exit with an error. This option requires curl 7.76.0 or newer.
limits.known: Looking up an existing repository through the shorthand route does not use the cold-create allowance.
limits.post: POST: 3 requests per minute and 50 submissions per day after URL validation. Failed verification counts toward the daily allowance.
limits.shorthand: Creating a previously unknown repository through the shorthand route: 5 per hour.
limits.text: Limits apply per IP. These are the deployment defaults; an operator can configure different limits.
limits.title: Limits and errors

prefill.honest: A design link is not a short link. Do not invent a slug or claim a link exists until qr2g.it shows it.
prefill.params: Parameters: repo, fg, bg, logo, ec, margin, radius, size, transparent and format. They match the asset endpoint. Unknown or invalid values are ignored and listed on the page.
prefill.text: Any chat or document can link to qr2g.it with a repository and design already filled in. Opening the link creates nothing; the visitor still presses Get link.
prefill.title: Prefilled design links

resolve.redirect: To inspect the normal short-link redirect without following it, print its response headers. Add -L to curl when you want to follow redirects.
resolve.text: The resolve endpoint returns JSON and verifies stale active links against GitHub. If verification is unavailable, it returns an error instead of trusting an outdated destination.
resolve.title: Check the destination

short.explicit: curl is recognized automatically. For another client, send Accept: text/plain or add ?format=text. Opening the same repository path in a browser redirects to its short link.
short.qr: Add ?qr to draw the QR code above the link with Unicode blocks, for a dark terminal; ?qr=invert suits a light one. Quote the URL so the shell leaves the ? alone.
short.sideEffects: This shorthand is not a pure read: for a repository qr2g.it does not know yet, it verifies the repository on GitHub and creates its link (5 per hour per IP; the operator can also require a browser check). Use the lookup endpoint below when you only want to read.
short.text: Replace smegg99/qr2g.it with owner/repo. A known repository returns its existing address; a new public repository gets one after a GitHub lookup. The response is a plain-text URL followed by a newline.
short.title: Get a short link

status.200: Existing link or successful metadata/resolve response.
status.302: A browser or short link is being redirected.
status.400: The JSON body or repository URL is invalid.
status.401: An automation token is required, unknown or revoked.
status.403: The repository is private, or Turnstile verification is missing or failed.
status.404: The repository or short link was not found.
status.410: The stored link is no longer active.
status.429: Your IP reached a request limit.
status.503: GitHub, Turnstile, or repository verification is temporarily unavailable.
